name: Mass estimator: integrating external calibration uncertainty

aims: Separate the cost of estimating noise from the effect of integrating its uncertainty, comparing all methods on identical simulated measurements.
Assess point loss, interval coverage, both miss directions, width and proper scores at fixed true masses; do not select a global winner.
data_generating_mechanisms: Newton II holds exactly. Independent isotropic Gaussian coordinate errors have true per-reading SD1 in each channel. Observe means of n=4 stable readings; within-repeat scatter is unavailable to inference.
Cross true mass {0.25,1,4} with per-reading acceleration SNR {0,0.5,2,8}. There are R512 independent deployment replicates per cell, with common measurement and calibration draws reused across cells.

Use k=4 or k=30 independent calibration vectors per channel. Fit a calibration mean vector and pool its three coordinate residual sums of squares: nu=3(k-1). Independent pooled SD estimates are redrawn per replicate and channel.

The two calibration-size experiments have independent seeds. Within an experiment oracle, plug-in and integrated methods use identical mass measurements. This does not study one calibration reused across many measurement experiments.
estimands: Fixed positive physical mass in each specified truth condition.
Expected bounded squared log loss and probability of a factor-two mass error.
Fixed-truth central-interval coverage, lower and upper noncoverage, mean log-width and distribution scores; 95% coverage is primary and 50% is diagnostic.
methods: The existing flat_joint plug-in law uses supplied pooled SDs as fixed. Preserve all existing comparator methods and their risk annotations.

calibrated_joint integrates separate isotropic channel variances with explicit independent scale priors d(sigma^2)/sigma^2, retaining the physical df d(alpha) dOmega reference measure. It uses reading means and external calibration only.
oracle_joint is the same flat Gaussian law supplied true mean noise SDs. It is a simulation benchmark with additional information unavailable to the other two methods.
Compare corresponding ratios of latent first moments E[f]/E[alpha], geometric points and medians. The arithmetic posterior mean mass does not exist; the ratio of first moments remains meaningful.

Check mass quadrature and calibration quadrature refinement separately on a fixed initial subset plus calibration and standardized-strength extremes. Numerical failures stop the experiment explicitly.
performance_measures: Point primary: min(log(m_hat/m)^2,log(2)^2) and fraction outside [m/2,2m], assigning invalid estimates maximal bounded losses.
Uncertainty: coverage at 50% and95%, both miss directions, mean log-width, log-mass CRPS, negative log density and interval scores.
Use paired flat-minus-comparator differences and their actual empirical MCSE within each cell, including coverage and proper-score differences. Across k regimes comparisons are independent.

Keep all R512 attempted trials. No performance-driven stopping, filtering or favorable-cell selection. Worst-case individual probability MCSE is2.21percentage points and paired probability MCSE is4.42points.

Null data contain no information about mass. Coverage near one preferred mass scale or a wider interval is not evidence of identification. Prediction scores relative to true force remain inapplicable at null.

methodology.title: Morris, White and Crowther: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
Murphy: Conjugate Bayesian analysis of the Gaussian distribution
Talts et al.: Validating Bayesian Inference with Simulation-Based Calibration
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions: Incomplete Beta Functions

interpretation: This fixed-truth frequentist performance study is not prior-predictive simulation-based calibration. The improper magnitude reference measure does not define a prior-predictive ensemble.
A conditional95% probability interval has no automatic uniform95% coverage guarantee across fixed truths. Integrating calibration uncertainty does not repair null identifiability.
This is an exploratory pilot of fresh pooled isotropic calibration, not the earlier six independent coordinate variance model. No paired comparison across those different studies is claimed.
Shared calibration across experiments, correlated/non-Gaussian errors, changing excitation and use of within-repeat scatter remain later extensions.
